measure: U.S. adults who identify as LGBTQ+

source.author: Jeffrey M. Jones
source.title: LGBTQ+ Identification in U.S. Now at 7.6%
source.population: U.S. adults age 18 and older; aggregated 2023 Gallup telephone surveys; more than 12,000 respondents

rows.estimateMethod: Nearest measured adult cohort (Gen Z, 1997-2006) carried forward; Gallup's 2023 estimate does not include these people as adults.

limitations: Gallup measures adult self-identification, not a person's romantic or sexual attraction, partner-gender preference, or behavior.

The survey category includes transgender and other identities; the cohort share is only a coarse population calibration proxy, not a claim that every non-heterosexual orientation has this same prevalence.
A stable seeded draw uses these aggregate shares only to create a private fictional identification record. It is not personal observation, diagnosis, compatibility, or a public stat.
Nonresponse is not imputed as heterosexual identity in the cited table; this implementation's two-way split necessarily folds nonresponse into the majority estimate and is marked low-confidence.
